label: IT Admin
description: Runs IT: the asset register (assets, their categories and tag policy, stocktakes), the asset desk (deciding requests and handing the kit over), and the IT help-desk queue. An employee first (`extends: employee`). Tickets are reached per category, not by a role rule: a ticket category that names `it_admin` in its servicing roles shares each of its tickets with the role. No platform or security access - accounts, roles, access rules, API keys, audit and the governance settings stay super admin's.
relies_on: The ticket-categories setting. A category's `roles` list is what gives it_admin the IT queue: services/ticketShares.ts writes a per-ticket role rule (`tickets.<code>.**`, write plus every verb) for each ticket filed under it. The seeded `it` category names it_admin; an org that renames or removes that desk moves the queue with it.

levels.why: Maintains the kinds of asset, and the tag code each one prints.
Decides these org-wide and hands the kit over (verbs below).
Inventory counts: the asset register being walked, by the administrator who maintains it.
The help-desk checklists, to pick one onto an IT ticket. Authoring them stays HR's.
IT setting: tag format, stickers, custody policy.

allow.why: Every asset verb: verify, print and reissue tags, batch create, lifecycle and restore.
Every custom verb on asset categories, including lifecycle and restore.
Open a count, record what was found on the walk, close it (and restore one deleted).
Hand over the actual asset, which is what closes the request.

excluded.why: A ticket's code is its requester's, so no scope token says 'IT tickets'. A role rule here would reach the HR and payroll desks too. The IT queue comes from the category's servicing roles instead (relies_on).

excluded.pattern: users.** | roles.** | access-rules.** | policy.** | api-keys.** | audit.**
excluded.why: Platform and security administration stays super admin's.

excluded.pattern: settings.access-approval | access-review | payroll-approval | sign-in | ai | attachments
excluded.why: Governance switches are super admin's, so the people they restrain cannot turn them off.
The help-desk catalogue decides which role services which desk, so it stays with HR: IT editing it could hand itself the HR queue.
